messages:
Maya R: FYI — ACME just opened an escalation: sudden p95/p99 regressions on endpoints that use tool/function calling with structured output. They say impact started ~10:15 UTC and affects production only. Logs attached in their ticket.

Maya R: baseline (last week) p95 ~220ms, p99 ~1.8s for their prompt -> tool flow. Now p95 ~480ms, p99 ~5.2s. Customer seeing large tail on tool_router path.

Maya R: @Samir K can you take a look? Customer is threatening rollback if we can't find mitigation in 2 business hours. :grimacing:

Samir K: on it. any repro or curl they gave?

Maya R: pasted the minimal repro in the ticket. i copied it below. includes structured_output validation turned on.

Maya R: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "oak-13b-fp16",
    "prompt": "Find best shipping option for order 123",
    "tools": ["rate_lookup","create_shipment"],
    "structured_output": {
      "validate": true,
      "schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "carrier": {"type":"string"},
          "service": {"type":"string"},
          "estimated_days": {"type":"integer"}
        },
        "required": ["carrier","service"]
      }
    }
  }'
```

Maya R: customer attached a span from their APM: ``tool_router.resolve -> validate_schema -> tool_invoke`` where validate_schema sometimes adds 120-300ms.

Samir K: thanks. initial hypothesis: our JSON schema validator used in the tool router is running synchronously on the main request thread and doing expensive deep checks + pretty-printing on big outputs. That could blow up p95 when tool responses are larger. Also there was a small change last rollout that added extra canonicalization to structured outputs.

Samir K: can you paste sample output from the tool? are they returning nested arrays or large metadata blocks that trigger expensive validation?

Maya R: customer sent one example output (trimmed):

Maya R: ```json
{"carrier":"FastShip","service":"overnight","estimated_days":1,"debug":{"route_steps":[{"lat":...,"lon":...}, ...]}}
```

Maya R: debug.route_steps can be big (~2-3k chars). they use full routing graphs in debug field.

Anjali P: that explains it. our validator iterates full payload and runs regex and type coercion in a few places. Deep nested arrays are costly. Also note we log the validated payload for audit which serializes it again.

Leo T: confirm there's a recent change in runtime that canonicalizes outputs for function-tool outputs (went out in canary last week). I see a PR that added toJSON normalization and then schema validate for all tool outputs, even if validate=false in some routes due to mis-check on config.

Samir K: can you point me to the PR/commit? we might need a rollback or fast patch that avoids serializing debug when schema doesn't include it.

Leo T: PR 7842 — added validate-on-every-tool in tool-router to prevent silent mismatch. It accidentally turned on for routes with structured_output:false because of a nil-check bug.

Samir K: ok remote repro: I'm running the customer's curl with --data-file and attached a simple profiler. Repro shows: tool_router entry -> call tool (avg 90ms) -> validate_schema (avg 220ms, that spikes) -> serialize/log (50ms) -> post-process (10ms).

Samir K: attaching profiler snippet here:

Samir K: ```text
[span=tool_router.enter] time_ms=5
[span=tool_invoke] time_ms=92
[span=validate_schema] time_ms=230
[span=serialize_audit_log] time_ms=60
[span=response_send] time_ms=15
```

Samir K: so validate_schema is the culprit.

Maya R: customer asks for mitigations they can apply immediately. any quick config they can flip?

Anjali P: short-term options:
- disable structured_output.validate on their route (if they can) -> fastest
- add filter to tool output to truncate debug fields before returning to router
- upgrade to a model variant with shorter outputs

Samir K: we can also add a server-side temporary toggle to bypass validation for big payloads (>1KB) or if schema only checks top-level. would need an infra hotfix.

Leo T: I'll open a quick deploy: add config flag `TOOL_VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES` default 4096, if output bytes > limit skip deep validation and emit a warning. That should restore p95 quickly.

Samir K: good. @deploy-bot kick a canary with that flag to prod region us-west-2 only. keep rollout at 5%.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for infra/tool-router with env TOOL_VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES=4096 on us-west-2, 5% traffic. rollout id: r-20260315-9001

Maya R: great — let customer know we'll push a mitigation and we need their permission for us to temporarily disable strict validation if they prefer.

Maya R: Customer update: told them we are investigating and have a mitigation candidate. they asked for a quicker workaround on their side while we deploy.

Samir K: customer-side workaround suggestions I want to send:
- add `structured_output.validate=false` for the route or for the call triggering large debug fields
- if tool returns debug, strip or compress it before returning to Redwood (e.g., return debug_summary only)
- set a per-tool output size cap in their adapter

Maya R: they said they can't change adapters quickly. they can toggle validate flag though.

Anjali P: also note we should audit other routes using structured_output — a small percent may be impacted. I'll run a query to find routes with structured_output=true and large median payload sizes.

Anjali P: quick query shows ~120 routes across orgs with median tool output >2KB, 18 of those are in prod for paying customers.

Samir K: ok action items:
- Leo: deploy canary with TOOL_VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES=4096 (5%) — owner Leo
- Anjali: run org-wide audit and produce list of affected routes — owner Anjali
- Maya: communicate mitigation to ACME and ask them to toggle validate flag if acceptable — owner Maya
- Samir: prepare a patch to short-circuit deep validation for large payloads and avoid double serialization — owner Samir

Anjali P: I'll DM infra with the list once query finishes.

Leo T: canary reports after 12 minutes: no errors, p95 for canary group dropped from 460ms to 240ms. Spike mostly mitigated.

deploy-bot: canary r-20260315-9001: 5% -> metrics: p95 238ms, p99 1.9s, error_rate 0.02%

Maya R: passing to customer: "we deployed a temporary mitigation that skips deep schema validation for large tool outputs; we're also ready to disable structured_output.validate on your route if you want an immediate knob to flip. Which do you prefer?"

Maya R: ACME: please do the server-side mitigation and we'll test. they confirmed.

Samir K: starting a patch to avoid serializing validated payload into audit logs when validate is a no-op. also adding fast-path: if schema is top-level simple types -> shallow validate.

Samir K: rough code idea (pseudo):

Samir K: ```python
# fast-path validator
if len(serialized) > MAX_BYTES: skip_deep_validate()
elif schema_is_shallow(schema): shallow_validate()
else: deep_validate()
```

Leo T: timeline update: canary healthy, I'll scale to 25% in 20m, then 100% if steady. keep monitoring p99.

Anjali P: I'll generate a post-mortem ticket and auto-assign to eng-runtime + infra. root cause likely was the recent PR enabling validate-on-every-tool plus lack of size guard.

Maya R: ACME confirmed post-mitigation numbers look back to normal. they will keep us posted if anything else. thanks team!

Samir K: we'll still ship the proper fix (avoid double-serialization + smarter validation heuristics) and a regression test to prevent future rollouts enabling validation without size guards.

Maya R: leaving notes for support runbook: add step to check validate_schema span in traces, look for validate_schema time_ms>100, and try temporary toggle or request infra to deploy TOOL_VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES.

Samir K: assigning follow-ups: PR #7894 (fast-path validator) -> reviewer Leo, target branch next-patch. Postmortem doc in incidents channel when ready.

Maya R: closing this thread for now. reopening if ACME re-escalates. :thumbsup:
